title: Observability-gated traffic quarantine with KV passthrough for active-active cutover
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During active-active edge cutovers we observe two classes of failure that harm live streaming sessions: (1) aggressive traffic shifts that trigger downstream overloads and immediate token loss for open streams, and (2) KV cache divergence during partial migration which causes model state mismatch and high error/retry rates. Existing mechanisms either drain traffic too bluntly (causing client-visible disconnects) or rely on full state sync windows that are too slow for high-traffic events.

Goal: Implement an observability-gated quarantine layer on the gateway edge that can: 1) selectively quarantine (isolate) a fraction of traffic from the cutover region based on real-time SLO/telemetry signals, 2) allow passthrough of KV-prefixed streaming requests (sticky prefix passthrough) so long-running sessions preserve their KV cache and avoid token loss, and 3) integrate a soft circuit-breaker that degrades non-critical requests before evicting streaming sessions. The mechanism should prioritize SLO preservation (99th latency and token-preservation for active streams) and enable deterministic rollback paths during cutover.

Why unique: Combines three controls in a single edge coordinator: telemetry-gated quarantine, KV-prefix-aware passthrough for session continuity, and a staged circuit-breaker ladder (degrade -> shed non-stream -> shed best-effort -> isolate) driven by SLO budget consumption. This reduces token-loss incidents while preventing slow surge-induced cascades in target regions.
acceptance_criteria: Gate evaluates SLO signals (latency, error rate, CPU/GPU saturation, KV miss ratio) and triggers quarantine policy within 10s of breach
Quarantine can be applied fractionally (1%..100%) and respects per-customer and per-route overrides
KV-prefix passthrough preserves inbound session KV reads/writes for pinned connections during quarantine with no more than 2% increase in median latency for those sessions
Circuit-breaker ladder enforces staged shedding: (a) degrade non-streaming to lower-priority model variants, (b) drop non-session background requests, (c) finally isolate region if headroom exhausted
During chaos test with 10k concurrent streaming sessions crossing cutover, token-loss incidents remain below 0.2% and 99th latency meets target SLO
Observability: dashboard exposes quarantine fraction, SLO budget burn rate, KV-pass metrics (hits, misses, passthrough count), and automated incident runbook link
Automated rollback: when quarantine disabled, previously passthrough sessions re-hydrate to target region without dropped tokens in >95% cases
implementation_notes: Architecture: add 'Edge Fanout Coordinator' service alongside gateway that subscribes to telemetry and evaluates quarantine policies
KV-prefix passthrough: implement prefix matcher at L7 that bypasses routing rebinds for connections marked with sticky-key header (safeguard with TTL and max-transfer-size)
Circuit breaker: reuse existing per-route token bucket but introduce ladder states and per-tenant grace windows
Telemetry inputs: per-region 95/99 latency, request error percentage, model GPU utilization, KV sync lag, and rate of streaming reconnects
Policy language: JSON policy objects stored in config-service; include per-route priority, max-quarantine-percent, and passthrough-prefix whitelist
Data-migration: KV passthrough requires short-lived cross-region proxy for reads; implement read-through proxy with metrics to measure consistency
Fallthrough: when passthrough TTL expires or KV mismatch is detected, gracefully notify client via structured event and route to fallback model variant
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (lab): unit/e2e tests and simulated cutover in staging (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (alpha): enable on 5% of edge traffic for internal accounts, observe metrics and iterate (1 week)
Phase 2 (beta): enable per-customer opt-in for low-risk customers across two regions (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (gradual): ramp quarantine capability region-by-region with telemetry gates and auto-rollback set conservatively (4 weeks)
Emergency rollback: global kill-switch at control-plane and route-level revert for passthrough proxies
telemetry_checks: SLO budget burn rate computed per-minute and per-route; quarantine triggers at sustained >20% burn for 3m
KV sync lag threshold: trigger passthrough isolation if cross-region KV replication > 500ms for >30s
Stream reconnect rate delta: if reconnects increased >50% relative to baseline during shift, increase quarantine fraction
GPU utilization high watermark: >92% sustained -> prefer degrade policies before shedding streaming sessions
Circuit-breaker health: confirm that shedding steps reduce request rate and headroom recovers within 2m
